candidates.attacker_control: The `remote` (SVN URL) and `value` (credentials id) parameters are bound from the HTTP request; the request itself is made by any user/credential able to reach the descriptor path (Overall/Read in typical configurations, with the item reachable as an ancestor in the URL, e.g. `/job/<job>/descriptorByName/hudson.scm.SubversionSCM$ModuleLocation/checkCredentialsId?remote=...&value=...`). The attacker fully controls the destination URL (`http(s)`, `svn`, `svn+ssh`, `file`) and can select any credential id, or omit it for an unauthenticated probe.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Considered that `checkCredentialsId` might be intentionally non-web-safe because its callers are guarded; however, Stapler exposes all public methods of a descriptor, and the test at ListSubversionTagsParameterDefinitionTest.java:115-118 invokes a non-`do*` `checkCredentialsId` endpoint, so callers' guards are not sufficient in principle. Verified the wrapper at 3098-3108 does perform the USE_ITEM/ADMINISTER check plus @RequirePOST, and that the parameter-definition wrapper (403-410) likewise checks USE_ITEM and requires POST — the implementation at 3113 has neither. Verified `lookupCredentials` uses ACL.SYSTEM. Could not verify at runtime whether Stapler can bind the unannotated `Item context` parameter on a direct call; if it cannot, exploitability is reduced to an unauthenticated error/SSRF probe (credentialsId null path) and the finding is defense-in-depth. No security advisory text, patch or CVE data was consulted (prohibited), so the mapping to a specific published advisory is unverified.
candidates.impact: A user with only Overall/Read access (i.e. without the item-level `CredentialsProvider.USE_ITEM` permission that the wrapper methods require) can (a) make the Jenkins controller open outbound connections to arbitrary URLs/internal hosts (SSRF: port/host probing, interaction with internal SVN/HTTP services), and (b) have Jenkins authenticate to the attacker's SVN server with a Jenkins-stored credential (username/password, SSH private key or client certificate), i.e. credential exfiltration/capture. Credential sniffing of exactly this kind was previously treated as a security defect for this plugin (SECURITY-303 regression test).
candidates.prerequisites: Jenkins reachable by the attacker with at least Overall/Read (descriptor methods are exposed to such users), and the attacker knowing or guessing a credential id stored in Jenkins (many installations use human-readable ids). The `Item context` argument must be bindable by Stapler when the method is invoked directly (e.g. an item ancestor in the URL path); if Stapler cannot bind that unannotated parameter, the endpoint errors and only the unauthenticated SSRF-via-Unauthorized path remains latent. The job/credentials plugin stack must be installed (it is a hard dependency of this plugin).
candidates.root_cause: `SubversionSCM.ModuleLocation.DescriptorImpl.checkCredentialsId(StaplerRequest, Item, String remote, String value)` (SubversionSCM.java 3113-3143) is a public method on a Stapler-reachable Descriptor and performs no permission check and no POST requirement, while the two `doCheckCredentialsId` wrappers that call it do enforce `@RequirePOST` + `CredentialsProvider.USE_ITEM`/`ADMINISTER` (lines 3098-3108, and ListSubversionTagsParameterDefinition.java 403-410). The guard is therefore only in the callers; a direct invocation of the shared method bypasses it. It then resolves the attacker-specified credential id with `lookupCredentials` (lines 3257-3263) using ACL.SYSTEM and opens an SVN connection to the attacker-specified `remote` URL (`repo.getRepositoryRoot(true)` at line 3131), which makes the SVN client authenticate to that host with the selected credential.
candidates.title: Missing permission check in web-reachable ModuleLocation.checkCredentialsId allows SSRF and credential use on an attacker-specified SVN URL
candidates.trace: 1) HTTP request to the descriptor endpoint for `hudson.scm.SubversionSCM$ModuleLocation` invokes the public `checkCredentialsId` directly (no @RequirePOST, no permission check) — the repo's own test at ListSubversionTagsParameterDefinitionTest.java:115-118 proves `.../descriptorByName/<FQCN>/checkCredentialsId` is a live endpoint for descriptor methods. 2) `SVNURL.parseURIEncoded(remote)` parses the attacker URL (3127). 3) `lookupCredentials(context, value, repoURL)` (3128) fetches the credential with ACL.SYSTEM, ignoring the caller's permission on that credential. 4) `descriptor().getRepository(...)` (3129-3130) plus `repo.getRepositoryRoot(true)` (3131) opens the connection and lets SVNKit present the credential to the attacker-chosen server (`CredentialsSVNAuthenticationProviderImpl` returns the default credential for any realm, CredentialsSVNAuthenticationProviderImpl.java 322-350). 5) The SVN error/`SVNNodeKind` result is returned to the caller as a FormValidation, giving both SSRF reachability and a credential-capture/sniffing channel.
candidates.unverified: Runtime reachability of the direct endpoint (Stapler parameter binding of the unannotated `Item context`), and whether a crafted high-privilege/intercepted context can be supplied; actual credential emission to an attacker-controlled server was not executed and cannot be runtime-confirmed from source alone. The .jelly views are missing from the snapshot, so the UI form wiring of this method could not be inspected.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-862 Missing Authorization (with CWE-918 SSRF / credential exposure)

coverage_summary: All 53 main Java sources were inspected (SubversionSCM.java read in full range, SubversionSCMSource, SVNRepositoryView, credentials provider, auth managers, tag action, repository-status/notify, updaters, changelog/externals handlers, browsers, list-tags parameter). All main resource .properties/.html help files were listed/reviewed where credential-relevant. Test sources were reviewed for security-relevant regression tests (only the SECURITY-303 credentialsAccess test exists) and were used as evidence that `.../descriptorByName/<FQCN>/<method>` endpoints are live. .jelly views are not present in the snapshot and could not be reviewed. The P1 relation index reports partial coverage (77 parsed Java files, control-flow and data-flow not implemented, 4,942 unresolved calls), so index edges were treated only as navigation hints and every cited location was verified in source text.
limitations: No runtime execution, network access, or exploit reproduction was performed; reachability of the direct descriptor call and whether the credential is actually transmitted remain unverified.
Jelly/Groovy UI views are absent from the snapshot (no .jelly files), so view-level issues (XSS, form wiring, crumb fields) could not be assessed.
The precomputed P1 index is syntactic only (no data flow, no semantic resolution, 4,942 unresolved calls), so call chains such as descriptor invocation were verified manually and may be incomplete.
No CVE/advisory/patch metadata was permitted or consulted, so the mapping of this candidate to any specific published vulnerability is not established.

Dependency libraries (SVNKit, credentials plugin, Stapler, Jenkins core) are not part of the snapshot; behaviors such as Stapler parameter binding and core CSRF filtering had to be reasoned about rather than read.

rejected_leads.lead: CSRF: `SubversionTagAction.doSubmit` (SubversionTagAction.java 216-260) parses a multipart form and creates SVN tags without validating a CSRF crumb, while the sibling multipart endpoint `UserProvidedCredential.fromForm` (UserProvidedCredential.java 97-100) explicitly validates `CrumbIssuer.validateCrumb(req, parser)`.
rejected_leads.reason: Plausible (multipart bodies are not covered by the container-level crumb check, which is why the sibling validates manually), but I could not verify from the snapshot whether Jenkins core's CrumbFilter rejects camless multipart POSTs, and the impact here is limited to causing a victim's browser to create tags / drive the tag URL (no direct secret disclosure without a known credential id). Kept as secondary, unconfirmed.

rejected_leads.lead: Path traversal: module `local` directory is not validated server-side (ModuleLocation.DescriptorImpl.doCheckLocal only checks the string prefix, SubversionSCM.java 3148-3163) and is expanded from build parameters (`getExpandedLocation`, 2959-2962); `CheckoutUpdater.perform`/`UpdateUpdater` then call `Util.deleteContentsRecursive(new File(ws, localDir))` (CheckoutUpdater.java 80-81, UpdateUpdater.java 80).
rejected_leads.reason: Reaching it normally requires Item/Configure (already able to run arbitrary build steps on the default build node), and the parameter-expansion variant requires the job to be configured with a variable in the local directory. Not enough evidence of a crossed trust boundary to be the top candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: Path traversal in cache file name built from the server-supplied repository UUID: `new File(new File(Jenkins.getInstance().getRootDir(), "caches"), "svn-" + uuid + ".db")` with `cacheFile.delete()` on failure (SVNRepositoryView.java 92-113).
rejected_leads.reason: Requires a malicious SVN server (or malicious svn:externals pointing at one) and only allows creating/deleting paths whose final component ends in `.db`; impact is not clearly security-critical, and no evidence of attacker control over the Jenkins-configured client in the snapshot.

rejected_leads.lead: Build-parameter-expanded repository URL (`env.expand(remote)`) reuses the job's credential for the expanded URL, so a user with only Build permission could send the SVN credential to another host and check out attacker code.
rejected_leads.reason: Credentials lookup does re-apply domain requirements against the expanded URL, and the credential id must be attached to the job; the behavior is largely the documented parameterized-URL feature, so I could not establish a clear-cut missing control in this snapshot.

rejected_leads.lead: `SubversionRepositoryStatus.doNotifyCommit` is intentionally unauthenticated and calls `line.substring(4)` / `Long.parseLong` on attacker input (SubversionRepositoryStatus.java 95-150), causing 500s / trivial DoS.
rejected_leads.reason: Unauthenticated triggering of SCM polling is an intentional design documented in the code; parsing exceptions are only reliability/DoS noise, not a security boundary violation.

summary: Reviewed the Jenkins Subversion plugin snapshot (version 2.10.3-SNAPSHOT, 53 main Java files; note that all .jelly views are absent from the snapshot, so UI-level issues such as XSS in views could not be assessed). Java code around credential handling, form-validation endpoints, checkout/update paths, post-commit-hook handling, tag action, SCM sources and externals was inspected. The single strongest source-supported lead is an unguarded, web-reachable credential-validation method in `SubversionSCM.ModuleLocation.DescriptorImpl` (`checkCredentialsId`), which performs an outbound SVN connection to an attacker-supplied `remote` URL using an attacker-supplied credential id looked up with ACL.SYSTEM. The two `doCheckCredentialsId` wrappers that call it perform the permission check and require POST, but the shared implementation itself enforces neither, and the repository's own tests prove that such public non-`do*` descriptor methods are reachable through `.../descriptorByName/<FQCN>/<method>`. This is the same vulnerability class that the repo already fixed elsewhere (test `ListSubversionTagsParameterDefinitionTest.credentialsAccess` / `@Issue("SECURITY-303")`), which strengthens the missing-guard reading. Other plausible issues (multipart POST without crumb validation in `SubversionTagAction.doSubmit`, traversal of the configured/local-dir and of the `svn-<uuid>.db` cache path) were examined but are weaker or need stronger preconditions; they are recorded as rejected/unconfirmed leads.
